evidence: verify_SABFI2_Gallardo_Pujol_2018_LOT.R re-runs all of this from the study's own Study 3 CSV (OSF kp572, osf.io/download/r2zhc), after tying that file to the live table (6/6 items n=419, means 3.03/2.83/3.22/2.44/2.55/3.56 match item_stats.R). (A) route 3, published totals: the postprint reports LOT Optimism M 3.33 / SD 0.83 / alpha .88 (N=419). Scoring {LOT1,LOT3,LOT6} as optimism and 6-x on {LOT2,LOT4,LOT5} gives M 3.330 / SD 0.826 / alpha 0.876 (|obs-pub| summed 0.008). Over all 20 ways to choose the optimism triple, the runner-up is the mirror {LOT2,LOT4,LOT5} (alpha 0.876 but M 2.670, dist 0.668 -- the reading where high resp = disagree), and every other assignment has alpha between -0.544 and -0.087 (dist >= 1.489). Gender subgroups keyed as claimed: 3.223/0.900 n=62 and 3.348/0.812 n=357 vs published 3.22/0.9 and 3.35/0.81. (B) route 6, keying polarity: 15/15 inter-item correlations carry the predicted sign; within-class r +0.46..+0.63, cross-class r -0.71..-0.37 -- the data are stored raw (not pre-reversed). (C) the study's own script scores keysLOT <- c(1,-1,1,-1,-1,1), identical to the LOT-R's scored-item sequence 1(opt),3(pess),4(opt),7(pess),9(pess),10(opt). ESTABLISHED: which three codes are optimism and which three pessimism, that values are raw, and that resp direction is 1 = disagree ... 5 = agree. NOT ESTABLISHED: order within a polarity class -- nothing distinguishes LOT1/LOT3/LOT6 as LOT-R 1 ('uncertain times') / 4 ('optimistic about my future') / 10 ('more good things') from any permutation of them, nor LOT2/LOT4/LOT5 as LOT-R 3/7/9; that rests on the deposit keeping canonical order, and neither the paper nor the deposit publishes per-item LOT statistics. Hence PARTIAL.
